6) On the other hand, learned counsels appearing for the respondents would oppose the submissions made by counsel for the petitioners.
They would submit that the lands of the fathers/mother of the petitioners were acquired according to provisions of the Act, 1957.
They would further argue that compensation was paid to the fathers/mother of the petitioners according to the notification issued by the State Government dated 04.08.2010.
They would also argue that the amount of compensation paid by the NTPC was accepted by the fathers/mother of the petitioners without raising any objections in the years 2014-15.

They would further contend that these petitions have been filed by the sons of the persons who accepted the compensation in the years 2014-15 without obtaining their permission or without impleading them as respondents.
They would also contend that the fathers/mother of the petitioners are still alive, therefore, the petitions are not maintainable.

They would further submit that when WP(S) No. 2387 of 2022 was filed, no plea was taken with regard to inadequate compensation and for the first time in the year 2022, these petitions have been filed without explaining the delay part.

They would also submit that Section 14 of the Act, 1957 deals with the method to determine the compensation and the amount of compensation was determined by the NTPC strictly in Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12818 accordance with Section 14 of the Act, 1957 and the same was accepted by the fathers/mother of the petitioners.

They would further state that the fathers/mother of the petitioners who accepted the compensation have not filed these petitions though they are alive, therefore, on this ground alone,
the petitions are liable to be dismissed.

They would also state that in the years 2014-15, though the petitioners were below 18 years of age, immediately after attaining the age of majority, they did not challenge the award of compensation made in favour of their fathers/mother.
It is also argued that the petitioners cannot blow hot and cold at the same time as their parents accepted the compensation without objection and they have challenged it.

The fathers/mother of the petitioners including the petitioners accepted the compensation in the year 2014-15; they claimed employment and in the year 2022, they filed these petitions claiming enhanced compensation according to the provisions of the Act, 2013 and the Act, 1957.
It is lastly argued that the petitions deserve to be dismissed.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the fathers/mother of the petitioners were owners of the lands as described in the opening paragraphs.

A proposal was sent by NTPC to the Central Government for the acquisition of lands and later on, notifications under Sections 4, 7, 9 and 11 of the Act, 1957 were issued pertaining to the lands of the petitioners along with lands of other villagers.
From agreements entered into by the fathers/mother of the petitioners in the years 2014-15, it is quite vivid that the amount of compensation was determined and the same was paid.
The owners of the property without raising any objection accepted the compensation so paid by the NTPC in the year 2014-15.

The original owners of the property are still alive and they did not avoid the compensation so awarded to them but after 7 years, their sons filed WP(S) No. 2387 of 2022 claiming therein employment according to the Rehabilitation Policy.

In that writ petition, there was no averment with regard to inadequate compensation and that petition was disposed of reserving liberty in favour of the petitioners to make representation before the appropriate authority.

The petitioners made representation before the officials of the NTPC and in turn, it was observed that the claims of the petitioners would be considered in accordance with the Rehabilitation Policy of the State.
Thereafter, the petitioners filed these petitions taking the plea that the amount of compensation was not paid in accordance with the Act, 1957.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners has stated that the compensation was not determined by the Competent Authority according to provisions Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12818 of Section 13(5) of the Act, 1957 but at the same time, the petitioners lost sight of Section 14 of the Act, 1957 which deals with method of determining compensation.
This section clearly says that where the amount of any compensation payable under this Act can be fixed by agreement, it shall be paid in accordance with such agreement.
Admittedly, the fathers/mother of the petitioners entered into agreements with NTPC and they accepted the amount of compensation.
They neither challenged the decision arrived at by the NTPC nor questioned the adequacy of the compensation so paid.

Though the petitioners were minor when the amount of compensation was paid, after attaining the age of majority, the petitioners did not file a petition challenging therein inadequacy of the compensation and in paragraph 7 of the writ petition, they have categorically stated that there is no delay in filing these petitions.
10) Sections 13(5) and 14 of the Act, 1957 would be relevant for the disposal of these cases and the same are reproduced herein below:-
Section 13 Compensation for prospecting licences ceasing to have effect, rights under mining leases being acquired, etc. -

(5) Where any land is acquired under section 9, there shall be paid compensation to the person interested the amount of which shall be determined after taking into consideration-- (a) the market value of the land at the date of the publication of the notification under sub-section (1) of section 4;
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12818 Explanation.--The value of any minerals lying in the land shall not be taken into consideration in determining the market value of any land;

sentences.text: (1) Where the amount of any compensation payable under this Act can be fixed by agreement, it shall be paid in accordance with such agreement.

(2) Where no such agreement can be reached, the Central Government shall constitute a Tribunal consisting of a person who is or has been or is qualified to be a Judge of a High Court for the purpose of determining the amount.

(3) The Central Government may in any particular case nominate a person having expert knowledge in mining to assist the Tribunal, and where such nomination is made, the person or persons interested may also nominate any other person for the same purpose.
(4) At the commencement of the proceedings before the Tribunal the Central Government and the person interested shall state what in their respective opinions is a fair amount of compensation.

Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12818 (5) The Tribunal shall after hearing the dispute, make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just, and specify the person or persons to whom the compensation shall be paid; and in making the award the Tribunal shall have regard to the circumstances of each case and to the foregoing provisions of this Act with respect to the manner in which the amount of compensation shall be determined in so far as the said provisions or any of them may be applicable.

(6) Where there is a dispute as to the person or persons entitled to compensation and the Tribunal finds that more persons than one are entitled to compensation, it shall apportion the amount thereof among such persons and in such manner as it thinks fit.
(7) Nothing in the Arbitration Act, 1940 (10 of 1940), shall apply to any proceedings under this section.

sentences.text: From a bare reading of these provisions, it is apparent that where the land is acquired under Section 9, compensation shall be determined taking into consideration the market value, damages sustained by the person and the fact whether the person interested is compelled to change his residence or place of business, the reasonable expenses thereof, the damage resulting from diminution of the profits of the land.

At the same Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12818 time, Section 14 of the Act, 1957 says that where the amount of compensation can be fixed by agreement, it shall be paid in accordance with such agreement.

In the present case, the fathers/mother of the petitioners entered into an agreement and the amount of compensation was duly paid in accordance with the terms and conditions of the agreements,
therefore, in the opinion of this Court, no case is made out to interfere with the procedure adopted by the NTPC in award or quantum of compensation.

11) With regard to rehabilitation/employment as claimed by petitioners, the NTPC is directed to consider the claim of the petitioners strictly in accordance with the Rehabilitation Policy of the State.

The petitioners are permitted to make representations before the Competent Authority of NTPC and in turn, the said authority shall decide the representations of the petitioners preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt of representation strictly in accordance with law.
The land owners/their legal representatives would be entitled to get employment or any other benefit available under the Rehabilitation Policy.
12) With the aforesaid observation(s), these writ petitions are disposed of.
